candidates.core_provocation: During a school memory test, every student gives the same account of what happened in a locked classroom—but the protagonist finds an earlier version of the answers in her own handwriting, describing something completely different. She realizes she secretly persuaded the whole class, including herself, to forget the truth, and the test is designed to make her remember.
candidates.why_interesting: The reader must discover both the hidden event and why a child would choose to erase an entire class’s memory.

candidates.core_provocation: The morning after a student vanishes, everyone at school remembers that he transferred, but the protagonist finds a video of herself helping him hide and a note from him saying, “Do not let them give me back my memory.” She must find him before the adults discover what the two of them have done.
candidates.why_interesting: The contradiction between the protagonist’s evidence and everyone else’s memories creates immediate mystery and danger.

candidates.core_provocation: A school offers students a way to erase one painful memory before an important exam. After using it, the protagonist learns that the forgotten memory is the only proof that her best friend is innocent, so clues left by her former self must lead her back to the secret.
candidates.why_interesting: The protagonist has deliberately destroyed the truth she needs, making every clue both urgent and potentially frightening.

parsed.reason_for_choice: The first idea is the most focused for a short story: it keeps the cast and setting small while creating two linked mysteries—what happened in the classroom and why the protagonist erased it. The memory test also gives the story a clear deadline and natural tension.
